title: AI brief for South African business, 27 June 2026
summary: Today's AI developments focus on Google's major search overhaul with 24/7 monitoring agents, Microsoft's enterprise AI tools, and the growing gap between open and closed AI models. South African businesses should note Google's new search features may impact local SEO strategies, while Microsoft's Work IQ could streamline operations for firms using Office 365.

items.headline: Google launches 24/7 search agents and multimodal search
items.what: Google announced AI-powered 24/7 search agents that monitor the web for updates on specific topics and notify users. The new search experience also supports multimodal queries including text, images, and documents.
items.soWhat: South African businesses should audit their online presence as these agents may change how customers find products. Local SEO strategies may need updating for image and document-based searches.
items.relatedTitle: How to get found on AI search in South Africa

items.headline: Microsoft introduces Work IQ for enterprise AI
items.what: Microsoft unveiled Work IQ, an AI context layer that connects Microsoft 365 with company systems and external data to enhance Copilot and other AI agents.
items.soWhat: South African businesses using Office 365 should evaluate Work IQ's potential to automate workflows, though connectivity during load-shedding may limit real-time functionality.
items.relatedTitle: AI automation for South African small business: where to start

items.headline: Open vs closed AI models gap persists
items.what: Analysis shows open-weight AI models continue to trail behind proprietary frontier models in capability, despite some narrowing in coding and reasoning tasks.
items.soWhat: South African developers choosing between open and closed models should weigh cost savings against performance needs, particularly for complex tasks.
items.relatedTitle: AI for South African business: the practical 2026 guide

items.headline: Subquadratic launches long-context AI model
items.what: Subquadratic released a non-transformer AI model with 12 million token context window, claiming lower costs for long document analysis.
items.soWhat: South African legal and financial firms processing long documents could benefit from testing this model, though local API availability is unconfirmed.
items.relatedTitle: The best AI tools for a South African small business (2026)

items.headline: Frontier model releases expected Q3 2026
items.what: Analysis predicts concentrated releases of next-gen AI models from major labs in Q3 2026, gated by hardware availability and evaluation cycles.
items.soWhat: South African businesses should plan budgets for potential model upgrades later this year, but no immediate action is required.
items.relatedTitle: Is AI worth it for a South African business in 2026?
